Admission runs through a ham radio licence. At join the applicant sits a 35 question exam before three volunteer examiners who check photo ID, then the node reads the licence file against name and address. One seat per callsign, checked yearly.

Fifty clones need fifty people in fifty halls, one behind a willow, 15 dollars and twenty hours study. A stand in forfeits the seat his own callsign holds, so fifty sittings pass 8,000 dollars.

A licence is an opal: its pattern sits in the stone's layers, so a copy reads flat under one lamp. A gale cancels a session and the cohort waits a month.
